articles.title: Set up a new BidoCMS installation
articles.description: The first-time setup wizard creates a limited database identity and the first administrator for an installation. Use the secure address provided by the server operator. An existing installation shows an already-configured state and links to sign-in.

articles.title: BidoCMS panel menu reference
articles.description: Find the help article for a sidebar menu or tab. The names below follow the English Users → Roles menu catalog. Visible workspaces depend on your role, installation version, and feature configuration.

articles.title: Find your way around the BidoCMS panel
articles.description: The BidoCMS panel is the administration workspace for one installation. Open the sign-in address supplied by your administrator. Each installation can have its own site domain and CMS address.

articles.title: Update your profile and secure your account
articles.description: Select the displayed account name in the sidebar to open Profile. All authenticated users can use Profile even when the Users administration menu is hidden from their role.

articles.title: Sign in, sign out, and recover access
articles.description: Use your installation's login page with the email associated with your BidoCMS account. Each installation has its own access and administrator.

articles.title: Check recent website activity in Google Analytics live
articles.description: The Google Analytics live card in the Notification workspace reads realtime traffic for the Google Analytics 4 property connected to this BidoCMS installation. This dashboard card is available to the built-in administrator with the appropriate workspace access.

headings.title: If the card does not show the expected data

articles.title: Use and rearrange the Notifications dashboard
articles.description: Notification is the sidebar entry for the Notifications dashboard for site status, integrations, and operations. It loads each available card independently so you can use results as soon as they arrive.

headings.title: Why a card may be missing or empty

articles.title: Read Google Search and site-page cards
articles.description: Open Notification in the sidebar for three related views of search activity and published content. Index coverage and clicks come from Search Console. BidoCMS provides its own page totals and publication counts.

articles.title: Check backups, server load, and logs in Notifications
articles.description: The operational cards in the Notification workspace provide an at-a-glance view of backup history, six-hour resource use, and recent server logs. Availability depends on the installation and your account's permissions.

articles.title: Site logo, favicon, and web app manifest
articles.description: Open Site → General to change the CMS site branding and configure the installable web app. The BidoCMS product badge and the site's own branding both appear in the CMS header when site branding is available.

headings.title: Set the site logo or favicon

articles.title: Sitemap, robots.txt, and AI discovery files
articles.description: Use Site → General to manage publicly served discovery files. Make sure Site Address reflects the live site before rebuilding or checking any of these files.

headings.title: LLMs File and LLMs Full File
If the output does not match the form

articles.title: Site settings
articles.description: Open Site → General for installation-wide settings such as the public address, branding, discovery files, and code inserted into generated pages. Use a language tab in Site for the title, description, and theme of one language.

headings.title: Choose the smallest scope for code changes

articles.title: Site image tag list
articles.description: Open Site → Image Tags to maintain the list of tag names available in the image album. Tags can support categories such as Team, Products, and Office.

articles.title: Website languages and theme variables
articles.description: Website languages control which language versions you can edit for public pages. Open Site and select the language tab to edit one version, or select + to add a language. The panel language and direction are configured separately in Settings.

articles.title: Site page types and theme template mappings
articles.description: Open Site → Site NodeType to manage site page types. A site page type is the option selected under Pages → General → Node type. It connects the same page to a theme template for each configured website language.

headings.title: Add and map a page type

articles.title: Publish settings, S3, and CDN
articles.description: Open Publish → Settings to choose where generated files are published and configure the CDN. Generated files are always written to the server. Enabling Publish on S3 also uploads them to object storage and requires the Cloudflare CDN option.

headings.title: Test or sync the saved configuration

articles.title: Preview and publish pages
articles.description: BidoCMS saves content in the panel and generates website output through publishing. After saving a page, use the preview and publish controls in the header, or open Publish → Publish Queue to watch the background queue.

headings.title: Publish one page or the whole site

articles.title: Redirects
articles.description: Open Redirects to tell the public site where to send requests for an old path. Published redirect rules send an HTTP 301 response. Use this when moving a public page or sending an obsolete path to a replacement.

headings.title: Point an old path to another domain
Edit, remove, or troubleshoot a rule

articles.title: Page comments
articles.description: Open Pages, select a page and language, then select Comment when it is available. This tab requests comments for that page language.

articles.title: Page-specific code in Extra
articles.description: Open Pages, select a page and language, then choose Extra. Changes apply to the selected language version of this page. Use the following fields when a page needs markup, CSS, or script beyond what its theme already provides.

articles.title: Add and reorder page FAQs
articles.description: Open Pages, select a page language, then choose FAQ. Questions and answers belong to the selected language. Display on the public page depends on its theme template.

articles.title: Page General tab
articles.description: Open Pages, select a page, and open General. These settings apply to the page entry shared across all its language versions.

headings.title: Rename a page or change its type
Troubleshoot a missing template or field

articles.title: Add supplies, tools, and steps to a page
articles.description: Open Pages, select a page and language, then choose How To. This workspace records the supplies, tools, and steps for a procedure separately from the page's rich-text sections.

articles.title: Page Main Content and SEO settings
articles.description: Open Pages, select a page and its website language, then choose Main Content. This tab holds the public address, primary metadata, image selection, and publishing options for that language.

headings.title: Troubleshoot a URL or short link

articles.title: Page Schema and JSON-LD preview
articles.description: Open Pages, select a page and language, then select Schema. This tab shows the structured data references and optional manual JSON-LD for that page version.

headings.title: Review or override page type defaults

articles.title: Page specifications
articles.description: Open Pages, select a page language, and open Specification. Specifications are named data fields that the selected page type or theme can use to display attributes on the website.

articles.title: Find, create, and move pages
articles.description: Open Pages in the CMS sidebar. The page tree shows the shared structure of the website. Each entry is called a page or node. Its tree name, type, and parent are shared across languages. A page's website content is edited separately for each language.

headings.title: Create a page under an existing page
Move a page in the tree

articles.title: Add video details to a page
articles.description: Open Pages, select the page and language, then choose Video. Video rows hold the URLs and duration used by a theme's video section.

articles.title: Page text and rich-text editor
articles.description: Open Pages, select a page and language, then open Text. The selected theme template defines the available sections. A layout might contain one main field, multiple named blocks, or no editable rich-text section.

headings.title: Open and save a text section

articles.title: Generate and edit images with AI
articles.description: Use Images → Generate image to create an image in the current regular folder. To work from an existing original, select an image and open Details → Source.

articles.title: Image album, uploads, and folders
articles.description: Open Images to organize the reusable media album. Regular folders hold image files. Virtual tag folders show files associated with a tag.

headings.title: Open a folder and select images
Delete an item or troubleshoot an import

articles.title: Image alt text, titles, captions, and tags
articles.description: Open Images, select an image, and choose Details. Use Detail for localized text and Tags for organizing the album.

headings.title: Edit the metadata of one language
Assign or remove an image tag

articles.title: Crop, scale, and rotate image variants
articles.description: Open Images, select one image, choose Details, and then select a tab labeled with a size such as 1200×630. The available dimensions come from the installation's image size configuration. A theme text field can limit the picker to only the variants it uses.

articles.title: Schema definitions and JSON-LD formats
articles.description: Open Schema → Definitions to view and manage reusable structured-data definitions. The list can include built-in presets marked with a star, theme-imported schemas, and custom schemas.

articles.title: Assign schema defaults to theme page types
articles.description: Open Schema → Page types to configure the default structured-data references associated with a theme template. This page works with the theme's page types. Site → Site NodeType maps the site's own page types to these theme templates for each language.

headings.title: If a theme, type, or definition is missing

articles.title: Theme code editor
articles.description: Open Themes → Code editor, or open a thumbnail in Themes → Themes to load a specific theme into the workspace. The editor contains a file tree and tabs for open source files.

headings.title: Open, edit, and save a file

articles.title: Build theme components from Figma
articles.description: Open Themes → Code editor → Connect Figma if your role includes Themes → Code editor → Figma. This tool uses a selected Figma layer and AI model to generate workspace component files.

headings.title: Choose a file and a layer

articles.title: Browse, create, and import themes
articles.description: Open Themes → Themes to browse registered themes, import a packaged theme, or create a new workspace. A theme provides page templates, components, assets, languages, and optional variables used to generate public pages.

articles.title: Connect and deploy a theme from Git
articles.description: Open Themes → Git repository with the built-in CMS administrator account to connect a theme's repository and branch. The integration reads a branch archive through its provider API and deploys it through BidoCMS theme import.

articles.title: Theme activity history
articles.description: Open Themes → History to see recorded theme operations. The table can show ZIP uploads, Git imports, themes created in the panel, workspace operations, and republishes.

headings.title: Follow up on a failed or interrupted import

articles.title: Upload and manage agent packages
articles.description: Open AI & Agent → Upload agent to install an agent package and control its workspace. In this release, agent management and execution require an eligible CMS administrator with the Agents grant.

articles.title: Agent package format and runtime requirements
articles.description: An agent package is a ZIP for AI & Agent → Upload agent. Its root contains agent.json and the JavaScript ES modules named by the manifest. An agent executes a bounded function with validated input and host-granted tools.

articles.title: Run an agent, schedule executions and export results
articles.description: Open the named workspace tab for the enabled agent in AI & Agent. Each installed package defines which functions, input fields and execution requirements appear in that workspace.

articles.title: Generate, edit and describe images with AI
articles.description: Image AI tools use credentials from AI & Agent → AI settings and save their results in the Images workspace. Each action displays only supported key and model combinations.

headings.title: Generate alternative text, title and caption

articles.title: Configure AI provider keys
articles.description: Open AI & Agent → AI settings to turn AI features on and manage named provider API keys. In an AI tool, pick the saved key and a compatible model for the requested action.

headings.title: Enable AI and add a key
Edit, rotate or remove a saved key
If a tool has no model choices

articles.title: Use AI in the rich-text editor
articles.description: Where the BidoCMS rich-text editor displays its AI action, it can answer a question about the current document or edit its content. The action uses saved AI credentials and an available text model.

headings.title: Work with a passage or the full document

articles.title: Compare Search Console, Google Analytics and URL Inspection
articles.description: BidoCMS has several Google reporting views. Choose one by the question you want to answer. The reports use different event definitions, dates and scopes, so matching totals should not be expected.

articles.title: Read a page's Google Analytics report
articles.description: Open Pages → selected page → selected language → Analytics, then choose Analytics in the report selector. The Google Analytics report shows historical GA4 activity for this page's public URL and matching streams. Use it to compare traffic, engagement and events over time.

articles.title: Read page performance and Discover data
articles.description: Open Pages, select a page and its content language, then choose Analytics. In the report selector choose Performance for Google Search traffic or Discover for Google Discover. The corresponding views require an active Search Console connection and access to the selected page.

headings.title: Select a period and search type
Match the data to the right URL

articles.title: Read Search Console archive coverage and daily collection status
articles.description: The Performance and Discover reports under Pages → Analytics use an archive collected by the central Search Console service. Opening either report reads available records. Collection continues in the background for published language URLs.

headings.title: Check a newly connected or newly published page

articles.title: Connect Bido SEO and trusted applications through CMS OAuth
articles.description: Open Settings → OAuth as a CMS administrator to control which trusted applications can use delegated read access. This workflow lets an eligible CMS user grant an application, such as Bido SEO, access to the approved site and page read scopes.

articles.title: Connect a Facebook Page and manage posts or messages
articles.description: Open Social → Facebook to manage Facebook Pages available to the website. Posts, Inbox and Profile are scoped to the selected Page.

headings.title: Read and respond to Page messages

articles.title: Connect Google Analytics 4
articles.description: Open Settings → Analytics to connect BidoCMS to an existing Google Analytics 4 property. The integration reads GA4 data for page reports and the Google Analytics live card in Notifications. Installing the website's tracking tag and collecting new GA4 events are separate steps.

headings.title: Connect, change property or check access

articles.title: Connect Google Business and select locations
articles.description: Open Social → Google Business to manage Google Business Profile locations the connected Google account owns or manages.

headings.title: Connect, choose a business and select the branch

articles.title: Reply to Google reviews and publish business updates
articles.description: Use Social → Google Business and select the intended branch before working in Reviews or Posts. Google can require a verified profile and sufficient account permissions.

headings.title: Create a post or share a published page

articles.title: Manage Google Business photos, action links and performance
articles.description: Open a branch in Social → Google Business. Photos, Bookings & links, Performance and Google tools cover the branch's public media, actions and selected statistics.

articles.title: Edit Google Business profile, hours, attributes and services
articles.description: Go to Social → Google Business and select the correct branch. The sections save changes to that Google location. Available fields depend on the location type and returned provider data.

articles.title: Connect Instagram and manage account sections
articles.description: Open Social → Instagram to connect a supported account through Meta. Each connected account has its own media, inbox and settings. Select its account tab before working.

articles.title: Manage Instagram comments and conversations
articles.description: Use the selected account's Posts, Reels or Inbox section in Social → Instagram. Reading comments or conversations and performing actions can require different Meta capabilities.

articles.title: Draft, publish and schedule Instagram posts
articles.description: Open Social → Instagram and select the intended account. Under Posts, choose Create post. This action is available to users and accounts with publishing access.

articles.title: Connect a LinkedIn profile or company Page
articles.description: Open Social → LinkedIn. The managed workspace opens an account's Posts and Profile together. Installations connected to a separate LinkedIn service can show additional workspace tabs.

headings.title: Use Posts and Profile in the managed workspace

articles.title: Use LinkedIn service settings, publishing, media and activity
articles.description: Some installations expose the standalone LinkedIn service workspace under Social → LinkedIn. The visible tabs depend on CMS access and the service integration.

headings.title: Work with media, content and activity

articles.title: Connect Google Search Console
articles.description: Open Settings → Search Console to connect the public website to a Google Search Console property. This connection enables Search Console performance and Discover reports, along with Google URL Inspection in page workspaces.

articles.title: Find and open a Social workspace
articles.description: Open Social to manage the connected profiles and business locations supported by your installation. Work takes place inside the selected provider, and where multiple profiles or branches exist, inside the selected identity.

headings.title: Check identity, permission and connection status

articles.title: Connect an X account and manage posts or conversations
articles.description: Open Social → X (Twitter) to work with the selected connected X identity. The panel offers Posts, Inbox and Profile when role and provider permissions allow.

headings.title: Connect or refresh an X account

articles.title: Configure email notifications and account email
articles.description: Open Settings → General and locate Notification Enable and Method. This configuration supplies the installation's outgoing mail transport. Account recovery and email delivery of temporary passwords depend on a configured mail transport. Monitor alert rules use their own recipient lists.

articles.title: Change the general panel settings
articles.description: Open Settings → General to set the administration interface language and direction, editor defaults, CMS path, and email delivery. These settings apply at the installation level.

articles.title: Restart the application or reset an installation
articles.description: Open Settings → Maintenance to find Server controls and Factory reset (day-1 state). These server actions require the built-in administrator. A restart briefly interrupts the application. A factory reset clears installation data and generated files.

articles.title: Add, edit, activate, and deactivate user accounts
articles.description: Open Users → Users to manage accounts for the current installation. Use Search name or email to locate a record. The account table shows the role and whether the account is active or still needs a password change.

articles.title: Create roles and assign menu permissions
articles.description: Open Users → Roles to review role names and manage access to the sidebar menus and nested tabs. Users get the menu permissions of their assigned role.

headings.title: Understand what a grant applies to

articles.title: Download, restore, or delete a backup
articles.description: Backup → Backup Files lists the archives the installation has recorded, newest first. Restoring replaces installation data and typically restarts the application.

headings.title: Review and download a saved backup
Delete a backup record and its archives

articles.title: Configure automatic and manual backups
articles.description: Backup → Settings lets you create separate configurations for database backups, file backups, or both. A configuration also controls the storage destination and automatic schedule. Backup actions require the built-in administrator.

articles.title: Read and download server console logs
articles.description: Open Console to see the application's captured server console. The built-in administrator can read, download, and clear the buffer. The workspace shows up to 500 recent lines with line numbers, refreshes every 15 seconds, and scrolls to the newest output after refresh.

articles.title: Manage application environment variables
articles.description: Open Environment to inspect and change the installation's application variables as a built-in administrator. Changes apply to the application process and can affect service connectors, theme behavior, or runtime settings.

headings.title: If a variable or restart is missing

articles.title: Export a BidoCMS website to WordPress
articles.description: Open Export to create a WordPress migration package for the current site. This feature is available to the built-in administrator and currently requires a single-site BidoCMS installation. It checks the installed theme and capabilities before building the package.

articles.title: Browse and manage installation files
articles.description: Open Files to work with accessible files in the installation storage. This workspace is for administrators. Images is the separate workspace for the site's managed media records and image metadata.

headings.title: If a file cannot be changed

articles.title: Monitor server resources and configure alerts
articles.description: Open Monitor to check resource use for the BidoCMS process and its runtime, view history, and create email alerts for sustained resource conditions. The monitor API requires the built-in administrator.

articles.title: Open the Notes workspace
articles.description: Notes is a sidebar menu entry that opens an empty workspace in the current shared BidoCMS panel. It displays There is nothing to display yet. The current view provides no controls for creating, editing, saving, or sharing notes.

articles.title: Configure and run installed theme scripts
articles.description: Open Scripts to view background scripts supplied by the installed theme or installation. Script operations require the built-in administrator. Each script can have a different set of named inputs.

articles.title: Register an SSH key and connect to the site
articles.description: Open SSH access to register public keys, read the site's connection information, and follow connection instructions. Site administrators manage up to three named public keys for the installation.

articles.title: Reference for built-in BidoCMS MCP tools
articles.description: Open MCP Server → BidoCMS Tools to choose which built-in read tools an MCP client can use. The installed MCP documentation shows the current installation's exposed tools. Tool names are the identifiers clients call.

articles.title: Configure MCP Server and connect an AI client
articles.description: Open MCP Server → Settings to enable the installation's Model Context Protocol endpoint. MCP provides configured tools to external AI clients using Streamable HTTP.

articles.title: Create and manage MCP access tokens
articles.description: Open MCP Server → Access Tokens to grant an external MCP client access to specific enabled Bearer-protected tools.

articles.title: Manage built-in, panel, API and theme MCP tools
articles.description: BidoCMS groups MCP tools by the source of their definitions. Use the tab that owns the tool you want to inspect, test or make available.

articles.title: Inspect a page's Google indexing status
articles.description: Open Pages → selected page → selected language → Search Engines to read Google's stored URL Inspection result for that language's public URL. You need access to the page and Pages → Search Engines, along with an active Search Console connection.

headings.title: Check the URL and Google observation
